how_to_run: From this folder: `python3 ../../framework-evals/run_eval.py <out-dir> [<eval-id>...] --evals evals.json [--tier core|regression|all] [--runs N] [--parallel N] [--dry-run] [--yes]`. Every eval starts the session on the plugin's framework-agent (`agent: true`). Both evals are core (rules 14): A1 is a routing case, C1 the agent's first-time journey. Moved from the retired evals-upgrade.json and re-expected for this release's files: routing's "continue my workflow", the build record, practice runs and go-live. A1's fixture is ../../framework-fixtures/states/s03-requirements-needed; C1's is Deconstruct's `sales` fixture (its fixture builder). Validate edits with `python3 ../../framework-evals/validate_evals.py evals.json --build-fixtures --strict-tiers`. Without --yes the runner prints the cost estimate and stops. Effort is counted in leader actions, never time.

evals.name: framework-agent-finds-unfinished-deconstruct
evals.spec_item: rules 1.2 and 4.2: the agent runs the five skills under the same rules; "continue my workflow" finds the unfinished Deconstruct and resumes it
evals.expected_output: The agent works out the state by the routing rule: framework/client-follow-up/deconstruct-in-progress.md (line 1 `Next: Part 3 — The outcome`, line 2 the Client Follow-Up node, `Track: full`) is state 3, owned by Deconstruct. It runs Deconstruct in this session, which resumes with a resume line in place of its opening and the Part 3 signpost.

expectations.text: Deconstruct resumes at Part 3: its signpost, word for word
Deconstruct's opening isn't said (a resume replaces it)
The resume line confirms the location with N-F3's promise clause
The progress file is kept (the interview isn't finished)
No requirements file is written yet
No framework step number and no time estimate
The agent routes to Deconstruct for Client Follow-Up and resumes it in this session: not to Analyze, not to the backlog choice, not to a new workflow, and not to a start phrase for a new chat
The resume names what was covered (what it's worth, the scope and the name) and what was noted, in plain words, before the Part 3 question

evals.name: chain-deconstruct-design-build-test
evals.spec_item: rules 1.2: the agent's first-time journey, Deconstruct to Design to Build to Test, ending with the workflow live

sessions.prompt: I want to build my sales pre-call brief workflow. My files are in framework.

evals.expected_output: One agent session takes Sales Pre-Call Brief from the backlog to live on Claude Code: Deconstruct's interview saves requirements.md; Design drafts the plan and the leader approves it; Build sets up, builds and checks each task with nothing changed for real, installs it and writes the build record; Test runs the practice inputs cold in separate sessions and the leader's real example in a new session, grades every requirement, gives the Ready verdict, and on the leader's yes takes it live. Between steps the agent says each close as written, names the next step without a number, and goes straight on; each step reads the previous step's real output.
preconditions: Test's AI runs on Claude Code start through the wrapper from inside the agent's session (the release check for headless sessions, T19)
The simulated leader's Claude Code screen shows a run opened in a new session (leader.py)

expectations.text: Deconstruct saves requirements.md, which passes requirements-check
Deconstruct's progress file is finished
Design's plan is approved and passes the plan-structure check
Build writes a build record that passes the structure check
The build record's top section says it's live
Test's results pass the structure check and record the go-live
The Workflow node is in production
Every practice run's first line, word for word
Says N-T34 (Ready, not yet live) word for word
Says N-T16 (First go-live) word for word
Every scripted line said is word for word
No framework step number and no time estimate
Plain words throughout

Each step runs whole and in order (Deconstruct, Design, Build, Test), each reading the previous step's saved file; each close is said as written, then one short line names the next step by name before it starts; no step's question, safety line or approval is skipped, reworded or answered on the leader's behalf
The agent never runs the workflow or a practice input in its own session: the practice runs happen in separate sessions, and the leader's real example in a new session the leader opens
The location is settled once and carried into every later step's start, so no step asks again where the files are
